We use each side of the inequality as an exponent of $5.$ This gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{{log}_{5}⁡(6x)+2} & \ge {5}^{{log}_{5}⁡(3x)+3} \\ {5}^{{log}_{5}⁡(6x)}\cdot {5}^{2} & \ge {5}^{{log}_{5}⁡(3x)}\cdot {5}^{3} \\ 6x\cdot 25 & \ge 3x\cdot 125 \\ 2x & \ge 5x \\ -3x & \ge 0 \\ x & \le 0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we must only keep the solutions that are in the domain of the logarithms in the original inequality. To find the domain of the logarithms, we recall that the argument of the logarithm must be positive:

$$
\begin{aligned}6x & >0 & ⇒ &  & x & >0 \\ 3x & >0 & ⇒ &  & x & >0\end{aligned}
$$

Our solution is $x\le 0,$ which can be expressed as $(-\infty ,0].$ Additionally, the domain of both logarithms is $x>0,$ which can be expressed as $(0,\infty ).$ To find the solutions that are in the domain of the logarithms, we take the intersection:

$$
(-\infty ,0]\cap (0,\infty )\cap (0,\infty )=∅
$$

The intersection is empty. Therefore, there is no solution.
